2. It was the case of the eviction petitioner - landlord that she had rented out the premises bearing Shop No. 15, in property no. 4415, Gali Bahuji, Pahari Dheeraj, Delhi-110006 to one Sh. Ramesh Kumar on 06.01.1987. However, the said tenant Sh. Ramesh Kumar had parted with possession and sub-let and assigned the same initially to one Sh. Ghanshyam Dass and subsequently to Sh. Bhagwan Dass, who were his father and brother respectively.
The current sub-lessee Bhagwant Dass was pleaded to be opening and closing the shop and dealing with the customers. It was also pleaded that the aforesaid Sh. Bhagwan Dass was a tenant in his independent rights of the petitioner in shop no. 6 in the same property and was using the shop no. 6 as godown and had shifted the counter from shop no. 6 to shop no. 15. Necessary permission for institution of eviction petition from the competent Slum Authority had been taken.
2.1 Petition was resisted by present respondent - tenant Sh. Ramesh Kumar and it was denied that the property had been sub let by him to his brother Bhagwan Dass. It was pleaded by the respondent that he is occupying the demised shop as a tenant and additionally conducting his business from shop no. 5765, Sikli Gran, Factory Road, Nabi Karim, New Delhi-110055.
As regards the respondent's brother Bhagwan Dass, it was further case of the respondent that his brother Bhagwan Dass was helping him in opening and closing the shop and dealing with the customers. However, it was denied that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was a sub tenant in the suit premises. Petitioner was pleaded to be receiving rent from the respondent.
RCT no. 52/2019
Smt. Promila Jain Vs. Ramesh Kumar Page 2 of 10 pages Digitally signed NAROTTAM by NAROTTAM KAUSHAL KAUSHAL Date: 2023.09.11 12:58:15 +0530
3. Petitioner in support of her case examined her attorney, Sh. M.L. Jain as PW-1, who supported the petition. Petitioner also examined two other witnesses, who were shopkeepers having their shops in the vicinity. Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was running the shop and not respondent Sh. Ramesh Kumar.
4. Respondent in support of his case examined himself as RW-1 and his brother Sh. Bhagwan Dass, the alleged sub-lessee, as RW-2. Both the witnesses deposed that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was working as an employee and drawing a salary of Rs. 10,000/- per month. The fact of Sh. Bhagwan Dass operating the shop and being in possession of key thereof was admitted. No proof of any other employee was produced. Salary vouchers of payment of salary to Sh. Bhagwan Dass were also not proved.
Payment register of the salary was also not proved.
5. Trial Court by the impugned judgment took the view that the fact of sub tenancy was not established. Trial court held that it was only a privilege or a licence by the tenant in favour of his brother to use the premises, which licence or privilege could be terminated at the sweet will and pleasure of respondent. Therefore, the arrangement did not amount to assignment or parting with the possession.
Further, it was the trial court's view that Bhagwan Dass was not a stranger or outsider but a family member of the respondent, therefore, sub-letting cannot be inferred.
6.1 Aggrieved by the impugned judgment, present appeal has been preferred. Sh. R.K. Jain, counsel for appellant has argued RCT no. 52/2019 Smt. Promila Jain Vs. Ramesh Kumar Page 3 of 10 pages Digitally signed by NAROTTAM NAROTTAM KAUSHAL KAUSHAL Date:
> 2023.09.11 12:58:26 +0530 that trial court committed a grave error in not appreciating the fact that respondent - tenant had for all intents and purposes given possession of demised premises to his brother. Respondent was running the same business from another premises in the vicinity. He had not been visiting the premises in question at all. Respondent's brother Sh.
Bhagwan Dass, who was also a tenant of the petitioner in another premises, was not operating therefrom and rather operating from the demised premises, which indicates that Sh. Bhagwan Dass had shifted his business to the demised premises. The story of respondent's brother Sh. Bhagwan Dass being an employee as put forth by the respondent and his brother was not established. Therefore, the possession of respondent's brother Sh. Bhagwan Dass is deemed to be in his independent capacity.
Another story, which has come forth in the testimony of RW-2, that tenant Sh. Ramesh Kumar had undergone angioplasty and was, therefore, not in a position to run the shop was neither pleaded nor proved by medical evidence. It is next argued that the matter is being pursued by respondent's brother Sh. Bhagwan Dass, who has been appearing before the Court even in the appeal.
> 6.2 Respondent's counsel chose not to address oral arguments despite opportunity. Written submissions filed by the respondent on record have been gone through; wherein, it is submitted that there is no error in the judgment rendered by the learned ARC. Respondent having parted with possession and not being in possession of the premises has been disputed and denied. It is submitted that Sh. Bhagwan Dass was working with the respondent as an employee for the last 20 years on monthly remuneration.

Electricity meter was also in the name of the respondent. In November 2018, respondent had undergone angioplasty and therefore, respondent had authorized his brother to operate the shop.
